meaning:
βαρύς, -εῖα, ύ,
[in LXX chiefly for כָּבֵד ;]
heavy: Mat.23:4. Metaphorical, burdensome: ἐντολή, 1Jn.5:3; severe (perh. impressive): ἐπιστολή, 2Co.10:10; weighty: τὰ βαρύτερα τ. νόμου, Mat.23:23; αἰτιώματα, Act.25:7; violent, cruel (EV, grievous): λύκος, Act.20:29.†
(AS)

elsewhere.note: For they bind heavy burdens that are grievous to be borne, and lay them on men’s shoulders; but they themselves will not lift a finger to help them.
For I know that after my departure, vicious wolves will enter in among you, not sparing the flock.
For, “His letters”, they say, “are weighty and strong, but his bodily presence is weak, and his speech is despised.”
For this is loving God, that we keep his commandments. His commandments are not grievous.
